verdict: Purchases up 50% this period, but revenue efficiency needs protecting now.
narrative: Over the last 28 days, your Meta ads returned a 4.8 return on ad spend (ROAS) on $1,483.04 in spend, producing 28 purchases and $7,120.96 in revenue — a solid base. However, while purchase volume jumped 50% week-over-week, ROAS fell 42% in the same window because recent orders are coming in at lower values, meaning each dollar spent is returning less revenue. Purchase momentum has also slowed in the last few days, with only 1 purchase recorded against roughly $137 in spend compared to 5 purchases over the three days prior. We're actively monitoring spend concentration — one campaign is absorbing 57% of total budget — and will protect the ROAS floor before extending any further scale.

highlights.phrase: return on ad spend across all Meta activity in the last 28 days
revenue driven by paid ads this period
week-over-week jump in purchases, though average order size declined

watch_item.issue: ROAS dropped 42% week-over-week as average order values fell, and purchase volume decelerated sharply in the last three days — concentration in one campaign is amplifying the risk.
watch_item.fix: Spend allocation across campaigns is being reviewed this week to reduce reliance on the single top campaign, and bid strategy will be tightened to defend revenue efficiency before any budget increase.
